transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. I, um, I hope I'm not wasting your time or anything. I just... well, I guess I've been having a bit of a hard time lately. I'm usually pretty tough—you kind of have to be, working as a heavy equipment mechanic—but, um... we started getting these foreclosure notices in the mail. 

And ever since they started coming, I just feel like I'm coming apart at the seams a little bit. I don't want to sound dramatic, but I've been catching myself sitting out in my truck crying before work, which is really embarrassing. And I jump every time the phone rings. I've even been snapping at the apprentices, and making these really stupid mistakes in the repair bay that I never would’ve made before. I just feel awful about it. 

Is... is it okay that I came in for this? I just want to make sure I'm doing the right thing.
Have you been having trouble sleeping lately?

Um, no... no, actually, my sleep has been mostly okay. I mean, by the time I get home from the shop, I'm usually so physically worn out that I just kind of crash. 

I hope that's okay to say? Like, I know a lot of people probably can't sleep when they're stressed out about money and things like that, but I really haven't noticed a problem with it. I always try to make sure I get enough rest so I can do my job right... well, try to, anyway. 

Is... is that normal? I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions right.
Have you been enjoying the things you usually like to do?

Um, well... I guess I haven't really been doing as much of that stuff lately. I mean, I used to love going to my fitness classes and volunteering at church, and I was always at the truck-club outings on the weekends. But recently, I've just... I've sort of stopped going. I don't want you to think I'm lazy or anything! I just haven't had it in me, I guess. 

And, um, at work... well, they actually took me out of the high-risk repair bay. Which makes sense, you know, with the mistakes I've been making. They're just looking out for everyone's safety, and I totally agree with them doing it. I just... I feel terrible that it had to come to that. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm not complaining too much. I know I should be doing better.
Do you still find pleasure in the activities you've stopped doing?

Um, well, I think so? I mean, I'm sure I would still like them if I actually made myself go. Like, the truck club is always a great group of people, and I know I'd probably have a nice time once I got there. 

I just... I haven't really tested it out lately, I guess. I don't want to bring anyone else down with my mood, you know? But I don't think I've stopped liking those things. I really hope I haven't. 

Does that sound right? I mean, I know it's not good that I'm staying home so much, and I'm really going to try to start going back soon. I promise I'm not giving up on everything.
Have you been feeling like you're a failure or that you've let yourself or others down?

Oh, um... no, not really. I mean, I definitely feel terrible about the mistakes I made at the shop, and I hate that I put my boss in a position where he had to move me out of my usual bay. But I wouldn't say I feel like a... a failure. 

I know I'm a good mechanic, usually, and I always try my absolute hardest to do right by people. I really try not to let myself think that way, because I don't want to be someone who just sits around feeling sorry for themselves, you know? I always try to pull my weight and fix my mistakes. 

I hope that doesn't sound arrogant or anything! I just try to keep a decent attitude about who I am, even with all the stress lately. Is... is that a normal way to look at it? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of answers.
Do you feel anxious most of the time?

Um, well... I wouldn't say *most* of the time. I mean, sure, I get a little worked up sometimes, especially with everything going on at the shop and trying to make sure I'm doing everything right. But I wouldn't call it, like, real anxiety. 

I really try to keep a lid on it and stay positive, you know? I don't want to be one of those people who's just constantly a nervous wreck and making everyone else stressed out. I usually just take a deep breath and try to push through it. 

I hope that's okay to say. I just don't want you to think I can't handle things, because I really am trying my best to keep it together. Does that make sense?
Do you often find yourself worrying about the future?

Um, no, not really. I mean, I try not to let myself get too caught up in all that. I know things are a little messy right now with work and everything, but I really believe things will work out if I just keep my head down and do my job, you know? 

I don't want to be someone who just sits around borrowing trouble from tomorrow. I always try to focus on what I can fix right now, today. I think that's the best way to handle it, right? I just want to make sure I'm dealing with this the right way, so I can get back to normal and not be a burden on anyone. Does that sound like a healthy way to look at it?
Do you feel like you've lost interest in things you used to enjoy?

Um, well... I wouldn't say I've completely lost interest. I still really care about my hobbies and my community! It's just... I guess I've stepped back a little bit lately, just to make sure I'm not overextending myself. 

Like, I haven't been going to my fitness classes, and I sort of stopped showing up for my church volunteering and the truck-club outings I usually keep up with. But I'm definitely planning to get back to them! I just didn't want to bring anyone down or be a drag if I wasn't at my absolute best, you know? 

And at work, like I mentioned earlier, they did take me out of the high-risk repair bay... which is probably for the best right now, just so I don't mess up any of the really sensitive jobs while I'm a little distracted. I really am trying to be responsible about it all and not cause problems for anyone else. Is it okay that I'm taking a little break from those extra things? I just want to make sure I'm handling this the right way.
How long have you been feeling this way?

Um, well... I guess it's been about four months now? Give or take. 

It started right around the time the, um... the foreclosure notices started coming in for the house. Which I know sounds really bad, but I'm working really hard to sort it out with the bank! I'm not just ignoring it or anything, I promise. I've been trying to stay on top of it as best I can. 

I just... I think that's when things started feeling a little heavier, you know? But I'm really trying not to let it affect my work or my attitude too much. I hope it's understandable that I'd be a little off my game with something like that going on. Do you think it's normal to be a little thrown off by that sort of thing?
Have you been having any thoughts about hurting yourself?

Oh, no, no, definitely not! I would never do anything like that. I mean, I know things are a little stressful right now with the house and work, but I'm not... I'm not giving up or anything! 

I really value my life, and I know I have responsibilities to take care of. I just want to get through this rough patch and get back to being the person everyone can rely on. I promise I'm not thinking about anything extreme like that. I'm just trying to handle things the right way, you know? That's what you'd want me to do, right? Just keep pushing forward?
Do you feel sad or empty most of the day?

Um, well... I wouldn't say I feel sad or empty all the time. I mean, sure, I have my moments where I feel a little down, but who wouldn't with everything going on, right? 

I really try to keep a positive attitude, especially at work. I don't want to bring that kind of energy into the shop. Sometimes I guess I do feel a little... drained? But I think that's just because I'm putting so much effort into fixing the house situation and trying to be a good employee. I'm really trying to focus on the good things, though! It's better to stay upbeat, isn't it? I'm doing the right thing by trying not to dwell on the negative stuff, right?
Do you feel like you're unable to experience pleasure from things that normally would bring you joy?

Um, no, I wouldn't say that. I mean, I still enjoy things! I really do. 

Like, I love working on the trucks at the shop. Getting my hands dirty and fixing a diesel engine, that still feels really good. I mean, maybe I'm a little more tired when I get home lately, so I might not have the energy to do as much on the weekends, but... but that's just because I'm working so hard, right? 

I still try to watch my shows or, you know, grab a coffee when I can. I definitely haven't lost my ability to enjoy life or anything like that. I'm just a little preoccupied right now. That makes sense, doesn't it? Anyone would be a little distracted in my shoes, wouldn't they?
Have you lost a significant amount of weight recently?

Oh, no, no weight loss! I mean, I haven't really been checking the scale or anything, but my work clothes all still fit exactly the same. 

I know sometimes people stop eating when they get stressed, but I've been making sure to keep my strength up. You kind of have to when you're wrestling with heavy equipment all day, you know? I'm trying really hard to take care of myself and eat right, even with the house stuff going on. I'm doing okay with that part, at least. That's a good sign, right? That I'm still keeping up with my meals and everything?
How often do you find yourself crying before work?

Um, well... I wouldn't say it's all the time. I mean, I guess it happens sometimes? It's just... ever since those foreclosure notices started showing up in the mail, I've just felt a little overwhelmed, you know? 

I try to keep it together, I really do. But sometimes, yeah, I guess I have found myself crying in my truck for a minute or two before I clock in. It's embarrassing to admit. I just feel like I'm coming apart at the seams a little bit. And I've been so jumpy, too—like, every time my phone rings, my heart just pounds. I've even caught myself snapping at the apprentices at the shop, which isn't like me at all. And... I've made a few stupid mistakes in the repair bay lately. Things I never would have messed up before. 

But I'm really trying to get a handle on it! I know I need to be professional at work. It's just a lot to carry right now, but I'm doing my best to push through it. That's normal, right? To have a hard time focusing when you're worried about losing your house? I'm not crazy for letting it get to me a little bit, am I?
Are there things that you used to enjoy doing, but now don't bring you any pleasure?

Um, no, not really. I mean, I think we talked about this a little bit already, right? I still really enjoy my work at the shop. I love getting in there and figuring out what's wrong with a rig. 

I guess maybe I haven't been going out with the girls from the shop on Fridays like I used to, but... but that's just because I'm trying to save money right now. With the house and everything, it just seems smarter to head straight home. It's not that I wouldn't enjoy it, I just... I'm trying to be responsible. That's the right thing to do, isn't it? Prioritizing my finances over going out? I definitely still like doing all the normal things I used to do.
Do you feel like you're unable to concentrate or make decisions most of the time?

Um, well... I wouldn't say "most of the time." I mean, I can still do my job and everything! Like I said, I did make a couple of little mistakes lately, but I caught them. It's not like I'm totally out of it or anything. 

I guess sometimes when I'm looking at a repair manual or trying to figure out a parts order, my mind wanders a bit to the whole... house situation. And it might take me a second longer to figure out what I need to do next. But I always figure it out! I'm still doing good work. It's totally normal to be a little distracted when you have big financial stuff hanging over your head, right? I mean, anyone would have a little trouble focusing with all that going on, don't you think?
Do you often feel guilty about things that have happened?

Um, no. No, I wouldn't say that. I mean, I don't feel guilty, exactly. 

I know the foreclosure thing is... well, it's a mess, but I didn't do anything wrong on purpose, you know? I've always worked hard, always paid my bills when I could. It's just that things got so tight lately. I guess maybe sometimes I wonder if I should have picked up more overtime, or... or skipped buying that new set of wrenches last year. 

But I don't sit around feeling guilty all the time! I'm just trying to fix it. That's the best way to handle it, right? Just keep looking forward and working hard? I'm pretty sure everyone has regrets when things go sideways, but I wouldn't call it guilt. That makes sense, doesn't it?
Do you feel like you're consistently unhappy even when good things happen?

Um, no, definitely not. I mean, good things still make me happy! Like, just last week, my boss brought in donuts for the shop, and that was great. I definitely enjoyed that. 

I'm not walking around miserable all the time, I promise. It's just... well, sometimes when something nice happens, I might smile and then right after, I just remember the bank notices and the house, and the good feeling kind of... slips away a little faster than it used to. But I'm not consistently unhappy! I can still appreciate the good stuff. That's a good sign, right? That means I'm handling things okay, doesn't it?
How often do you feel sad or empty during the day?

Um, I wouldn't say I feel sad or empty, really. I mean, I'm just stressed! 

I guess there are moments... you know, maybe during my lunch break or when I first wake up, where I feel a little heavy? Like, just tired from dealing with everything. But I wouldn't call it empty. I'm still getting up and going to work every day, still turning wrenches and getting the job done. 

I'm pretty sure anyone would feel a little down when they're worried about losing their home, right? It's just a normal reaction to a tough spot. I'm definitely not sitting around crying all day or anything like that. That's what you're asking, right? I'm doing my best to stay positive about it all.
Do you feel like you're a burden to others?

Oh, no. No, I really try hard not to be! I mean, I don't think I am. I keep pretty much all of this... this whole situation with the house to myself. I definitely don't want to drag my friends or family down with my stress, you know? 

I've always been the kind of person who takes care of her own problems. I fix heavy equipment for a living, so... I guess I just try to fix my own messes, too. I don't go around complaining or asking anyone for handouts. I just put my head down and keep working. That's the right way to handle it, isn't it? Just making sure you're not putting your problems on anyone else?
